name: lipoprotein_transport
description: Lipoprotein-mediated transport of cholesterol and triglycerides. VLDL carries cholesterol out of the liver; LDL delivers it to tissues; HDL performs reverse cholesterol transport back to the liver.

nodes.label: Chylomicron
nodes.notes: Intestine-derived. Carries dietary fat and cholesterol. ApoB-48.

nodes.label: VLDL (Very Low Density Lipoprotein)
nodes.notes: Liver-derived. Carries endogenously synthesized triglycerides and cholesterol. ApoB-100.

nodes.label: IDL (Intermediate Density Lipoprotein)
nodes.notes: Remnant of VLDL after partial triglyceride removal by lipoprotein lipase.

nodes.label: LDL (Low Density Lipoprotein)
nodes.notes: Major cholesterol-carrying particle in plasma. Delivers cholesterol to peripheral tissues via LDL receptor. Elevated LDL is a major risk factor for atherosclerosis.

nodes.label: HDL (High Density Lipoprotein)
nodes.notes: Reverse cholesterol transport particle. Collects excess cholesterol from peripheral cells and returns it to the liver (for excretion as bile acids or biliary cholesterol).

nodes.label: Peripheral Cell
nodes.notes: Extrahepatic cells that take up LDL cholesterol for membrane synthesis or steroidogenesis.

nodes.label: Liver
nodes.notes: Central organ of cholesterol homeostasis. Synthesizes cholesterol, packages it into VLDL, and excretes it via bile.

edges.notes: Liver packages triglycerides + cholesterol esters + ApoB-100 into VLDL particles.
Progressive removal of triglycerides converts VLDL → IDL → LDL.
Final conversion to the cholesterol-rich LDL particle.
Primary route of cholesterol delivery to extrahepatic tissues. Defects in this receptor cause familial hypercholesterolemia.
Reverse cholesterol transport begins. Free cholesterol is transferred to nascent HDL and esterified by LCAT.
HDL delivers cholesterol back to the liver for excretion into bile or conversion to bile acids.
